phases.name: Walking Skeleton — boot, discover Ollama, browse, zap, see reclaim
phases.description: Thinnest end-to-end vertical slice that proves the architecture: TUI launches with two-pane ratatui layout, Ollama plugin discovers real on-disk models via the Tool trait, user navigates panes, zaps the whole tool with typed-name confirmation, and sees a post-action reclaim message. Walking-skeleton exit gate = the 22 scenarios tagged @walking-skeleton in master-acceptance.feature go green. Closes the riskiest assumption (we can correctly read a tool's on-disk layout AND mutate it safely) before any other plugin or unify work begins.
phases.exit_gate: All scenarios tagged @walking-skeleton in docs/feature/modeltap-tui/distill/features/master-acceptance.feature pass on macOS and Linux CI runners.

steps.name: US-01: TUI launches and quits cleanly (workspace + ratatui foundation)
steps.description: Foundation step. Stand up the cargo workspace (crates/modeltap-core, crates/modeltap-tui, crates/modeltap-app), bring in ratatui+crossterm+tokio per ADR-005/006, wire the GitHub Actions CI workflow from devops/ci-pipeline.md (macOS-latest + ubuntu-latest matrix, cargo fmt/clippy/test/deny), add cargo-deny.toml for OSS-license enforcement, and ship the smallest binary that paints the empty two-pane layout, restores the terminal on q/Ctrl+C, and refuses to start when the terminal is narrower than 80 columns. Implements panic hook that restores terminal state before printing per ADR-006. Right-pane data is intentionally a 'discovering...' placeholder; real Ollama data lands in 01-02. Tests use ratatui::backend::TestBackend + insta for snapshot frames; headless-mode flag is added so acceptance tests can drive the binary without a real PTY.
criteria: Cold start to first paint completes in under 1 second on a 2020-or-later workstation (US-01.AC-1)
Pressing q exits with code 0 and restores terminal cursor and color state (US-01.AC-2)
Pressing Ctrl+C exits with code 130 and restores terminal state (US-01.AC-3)
Terminal narrower than 80 columns is detected and refused with usage error 'Terminal too narrow: need at least 80 columns, found N' on stderr and exit code 2 (US-01.AC-4)
No escape-sequence garbage left on screen after exit in any tested terminal emulator (US-01.AC-5)
Bottom bar shows '[<-/->] tools  [up/down] models  [u] unify  [z] zap tool  [?] help  [q] quit' on first paint

If ~/.modeltap/ logging directory is unwritable, modeltap renders the TUI and warns to stderr but does not crash. Logs (launch.log, diagnostics.log) are operational only — their absence does not affect discovery, mutations, or correctness (per intake Q7 + ADR-003 stateless guarantee)

steps.name: US-02: Discover real Ollama models (Tool trait + plugin registration)
steps.description: Defines the Tool trait in modeltap-core (the public plugin port frozen by ADR-001 — name, accepted_formats, discover, link, delete_one, delete_all) and ships the first concrete implementation: the Ollama plugin. Walks ~/.ollama/models/manifests/ recursively, resolves blob references in ~/.ollama/models/blobs/sha256-*, and produces DiscoveredModel entries with id, size, format, on-disk path, and a lazy SHA256 (None at this stage). Self-registers via the inventory crate per ADR-001 — modeltap-app/src/registry.rs collects all submitted plugin instances at startup. Replaces the 'discovering...' placeholder from 01-01 with real rows. Missing ~/.ollama/ is reported as '(not installed)'; unreadable directory is reported as '(error)' with a structured event in diagnostics.log; one bad plugin must NOT crash the TUI (panic isolation via tokio::task::spawn + JoinError).

steps.name: US-05: Zap-all with typed-name confirmation modal
steps.description: Adds the first destructive action to the walking skeleton: pressing 'z' on a selected tool opens a modal showing model count, total bytes, unique-vs-shared breakdown (computed conservatively per ADR-002 — uncertain dedup keys treat as unique), and requires the user to type the tool name exactly (case-sensitive). Esc cancels at any point. On confirm, calls Tool::delete_all on the selected plugin (ADR-009 separates this from delete_one). For the WS slice, 'shared' detection uses the in-process inventory only (compatibility engine arrives in 02-05); for now the unique-vs-shared count is conservative — all models are treated as unique unless an exact same-path duplicate exists across plugins. Empty tools surface a benign 'Nothing to zap' message. Emits JSONL action.zap_all event.

steps.name: US-06: Post-action message with reclaim/retain breakdown
steps.description: After any mutating action (zap in WS scope; unify added in 03-02; delete-from-one in 03-06), the right pane displays 'Last action: <verb> <target> (<status>)' header and 'Reclaimed: <N> GB (<M> GB retained — also linked from other tools)' body. The summary bar refreshes total disk usage within 500ms via incremental rediscovery of the affected tool. Last-action message clears when the user navigates to a different tool. Partial-success path is wired in but only exercised by 03-02/03-03 scenarios (cross-fs); for WS, only success and full-failure outcomes are reachable.

phases.name: Make duplication visible — full inventory across 4 tools, indicators, detail screen
phases.description: Builds out the other three plugins (llama-cli, Hugging Face, LM Studio) so the cross-tool view is real, then adds the row metadata format, the compatibility indicator engine (the o/*/!/? badges), the model detail screen, and the format-locked red ! signal. After Phase 02, Devon can answer 'how much could I reclaim?' without unifying anything — a valuable diagnostic on its own. Also includes the LM Studio path-convention verification spike (per DESIGN ADR-004 / OQ-2) folded into 02-04 as discovery-only scope.

steps.name: US-04: Row metadata format (indicator + size + 'also in:' annotation)
steps.description: Defines the canonical row format used by every tool's right-pane list: '<indicator> <model id>  <size>  also in: <other tools>' where indicator is one of {o, *, !, ?}. In this step the indicator is a STATIC placeholder driven only by simple presence-counting (model present in 2+ tools => '*', else 'o', '?' if format unparseable); the real format-aware engine arrives in 02-05. Color rules per US-04.AC-3: o/* neutral, ! red, ? yellow — paired with the symbol per WCAG so NO_COLOR-compliant. 'also in: ...' annotation is rendered only for *-marked rows.

steps.name: US-07: llama-cli plugin — discover loose .gguf files with header parsing
steps.description: Second concrete Tool implementation. steps.name: US-12: Hugging Face plugin — walk hub/ snapshot symlink farm
steps.description: Third concrete Tool implementation, and the most complex discovery — HF cache uses a symlink farm: ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--<org>--<repo>/snapshots/<rev>/<file> -> ../../blobs/<sha256>. Walks every models--*/snapshots/<rev>/ directory, resolves snapshot symlinks to their blob targets, and produces Model entries with id = '<org>/<repo>' (path-style canonical), format inferred from filename suffix (.gguf, .safetensors, .bin, .awq). Honors HF_HOME env var override. Broken snapshot symlinks are reported with [broken: missing blob] and excluded from disk-usage totals — never silent. accepted_formats() returns the union of formats HF can host (gguf, safetensors, bin, awq, ...). This step also performs the HF linking spike documented in ADR-004 OQ-1 — verifying that replacing the snapshot symlink target (or replacing the blob in place via hardlink) is feasible — and records the conclusion in a CR (code review) note for use by 03-02.

steps.name: US-09: Compatibility indicator engine (pure fn over plugin accepted_formats)
steps.description: Replaces the static placeholder indicator from 02-01 with a real, format-aware computation. Pure function in modeltap-core::logic::compatibility: compute_indicator(model, &registered_plugins) -> Indicator. Star (*) when the model is currently in 2+ tools matched by SHA256 dedup key (per ADR-002, with conservative fallback to HF repo+quant when SHA256 not yet computed). Open (o) when the model is in only 1 tool but at least one OTHER registered plugin's accepted_formats() accepts the model's format. Bang (!) when the model is in only 1 tool and no other plugin accepts its format. Question (?) when format is unknown OR a plugin's accepted_formats() is empty. Recomputed after every zap/unify (US-09.AC-4). Now needs all four plugins from 02-02..02-04 to ship a meaningful matrix.

phases.name: Reclaim disk space safely — unify, dry-run, single-model delete, cross-fs, running-tool detect
phases.description: Phase 03 delivers the value proposition: cross-tool unification via hardlinks, with safety guardrails (dry-run, cross-fs fallback, running-tool detect-and-prompt-then-retry per intake Q5). Includes single-model delete (US-05b) per the F4 intake update and ADR-009. Largest phase by hours; 03-02 (US-10 unify) is the single largest step in the roadmap because per-tool linking semantics (Ollama blob layout, llama-cli loose .gguf, HF symlink farm, LM Studio config) are all distinct and each plugin's link() method must be correct.

steps.name: US-10: Unify via hardlinks (per-tool link() implementations)
steps.description: The keystone step of the entire project. Implements Tool::link() for all four plugins: (1) Ollama — replace ~/.ollama/models/blobs/sha256-<hash> with a hardlink to the chosen canonical (only if Ollama's blob hash equals the file's SHA256 of content bytes — verified by OQ-3 spike at the start of this step); (2) llama-cli — replace the loose .gguf file at its path with a hardlink to canonical; (3) HF — replace the snapshot symlink target (the blob in .cache/huggingface/hub/blobs/) with a hardlink to canonical, per the ADR-004 spike result captured in 02-03; (4) LM Studio — replace the model file in place with a hardlink to canonical, per the ADR-004 spike result from 02-04. The composition root selects the canonical based on the rule: largest existing copy wins (or the content-addressed Ollama blob if available — typically these are the same). NO ~/.modeltap/store/ is created (intake Q1, ADR-003). The unify dialog shows the chosen canonical, the hardlink targets, and the disk reclaim BEFORE Enter. Already-unified models (all paths same inode) show a benign info message. Sequence per ADR-008: (a) verify same-fs (or fall back per 03-03), (b) create canonical hardlink at sibling path, (c) atomic rename over the existing path, (d) update tool manifest. Steps 1-3 roll back on step 4 failure. Emits JSONL action.unify event.

steps.name: US-19: Cross-filesystem fallback (refuse-default with per-target choice)
steps.description: Hooks the EXDEV (cross-filesystem hardlink) error from 03-02 into a per-target choice dialog. Filesystem check uses stat device IDs via the FsProbe port (defined in modeltap-core/src/ports.rs in 03-02). When all targets are same-fs as canonical, unify proceeds normally (no prompt). When 1+ target is on a different filesystem, dialog reads 'N of M targets on different filesystem' and offers '[s] skip cross-fs / [c] copy / [x] cancel'. Skip leaves the cross-fs target untouched. Copy duplicates bytes (no reclaim for that target) and reports 'Copied: N cross-fs target(s) (no reclaim)' in the post-action summary. All targets cross-fs: dialog reads 'all targets on different filesystems — unify cannot proceed' and refuses. Default policy = refuse-and-ask per ADR-008 / OQ-4 (no silent copy that wastes disk).

steps.name: US-05b: Single-model delete via Tool::delete_one (per ADR-009)
steps.description: Implements the [d] shortcut on the model detail screen, dispatching to Tool::delete_one (a first-class trait method per ADR-009 — NOT a special case of zap). Confirmation rule splits on shared-vs-unique: if the model is shared with other tools (compatibility engine reports >1 compatible tool currently registered), use single-key [y/n] confirmation (low friction — content is preserved elsewhere); if the model is UNIQUE to this tool (the only copy), require typed-id confirmation matching the safety bar of US-05. Esc cancels at any point. After deletion, only the targeted tool's registration/file is removed; other tools' copies (if any) remain unaffected and still openable. If the targeted tool is running and holds the file open, surface 'close <tool> and retry' per intake Q5 (this branch fully wired by 03-07; for this step the running-tool check is a stub returning 'no running tools' — 03-07 plugs it in). Emits JSONL action.zap_one event with was_shared bool.

steps.name: US-17: Detect-and-prompt-then-retry for running tools (per intake Q5)
steps.description: Implements the FsProbe::detect_running_tools() port using lsof on macOS/Linux (cfg!(unix) gated). Before any unify or single-model delete (zap-all already proceeds without this gate per intake Q5 wording), modeltap checks whether any registered plugin's tool process holds in-scope files open. If yes, dialog reads '<tool> is running and has this file open. Close <tool> and retry.' offering [r] retry / [Esc] cancel. NO partial mutation occurs while the dialog is open — this is detect-and-prompt-then-retry per Q5 (NOT soft-warning, which was the pre-Q5 stance). On [r] after the user closes the tool, the action proceeds normally. If lsof is unavailable (stripped container), the dialog says 'Running-tool detection unavailable on this system' and Devon can proceed at his own risk. Detection completes within 500ms.

steps.name: US-18: Plugin trait certification (CONTRIBUTING.md, panic isolation, architecture lint)
steps.description: Certifies the Tool trait already shipped in 01-02. Three deliverables: (1) CONTRIBUTING.md with a worked example walking Riley Chen through implementing an Atomic Chat plugin (the 5th tool) — must include the inventory::submit! registration line and explain how the trait surface is frozen at SemVer-major boundaries. (2) Plugin panic isolation hardening: every plugin call wrapped in tokio::task::spawn + JoinError; a panicking plugin shows '(error)' in left pane and writes panic_message to diagnostics.log without crashing the TUI (already partly wired in 01-02; this step adds the explicit @plugin-trait test). (3) Architecture rule R1 enforcement per ci-pipeline.md §4: tests/architecture.rs parses cargo metadata --format-version 1 JSON and asserts (a) modeltap-core has no path-deps on plugins, (b) plugins do not depend on each other, (c) modeltap-tui does not import any concrete plugin. The test runs in CI as a gating job. Includes a 5th-plugin fixture (riley-fifth-plugin) that exists ONLY as a test fixture proving the contract.
